**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/21 (Sun) 10:10
- [FACT] User is familiar with meaning-for-meaning transcription.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Meaning-for-meaning transcription is a method of transcribing spoken language in real-time for individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Meaning-for-meaning transcription focuses on conveying the overall meaning and intent of the spoken message rather than providing a verbatim transcription.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] TypeWell and C-Print are two well-known service providers that offer meaning-for-meaning transcription.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] TypeWell uses trained transcribers to provide real-time, meaning-for-meaning transcriptions of lectures, meetings, and other events.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] TypeWell transcribers use abbreviation software to help them keep up with the speed of spoken language.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] TypeWell aims to convey the essential meaning of what is being said while maintaining a high level of accuracy and readability.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] C-Print is another meaning-for-meaning transcription service that also uses trained transcribers to provide real-time transcriptions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] C-Print transcribers use a phonetic-based abbreviation system to capture the essence of spoken language quickly and efficiently.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] C-Print is designed to provide clear and accurate transcriptions that focus on conveying the overall meaning and intent of the spoken message.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Both TypeWell and C-Print services are commonly used in educational settings to provide communication access for deaf or hard of hearing students.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] TypeWell and C-Print can also be used in various other settings such as conferences, meetings, and presentations.
